name: Depth Anything V2
plain: Depth Anything V2: relative depth from one image, in small, base and large. The licence differs by size, see the table.
summary: Depth Anything V2 (Yang et al. 2024): relative monocular depth from a DINOv2 ViT encoder and a DPT head, trained on synthetic labels and 62M pseudo-labelled real images; with the authors' metric fine-tunes (Hypersim indoor, Virtual KITTI 2 outdoor) and the Distill-Any-Depth checkpoints (He et al. 2025) of the same network.

papers.title: Distill Any Depth: Distillation Creates a Stronger Monocular Depth Estimator

licence_notes: Only the Small weights are Apache-2.0; the Base and Large weights are CC-BY-NC-4.0. The training data of even the Small model has unclear commercial terms (a note only).

The six metric checkpoints are Apache-2.0 on their Hugging Face cards, but the Base / Large ones are fine-tuned from the CC-BY-NC-4.0 relative Base / Large weights, and Virtual KITTI 2 (the outdoor fine-tune) is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, Hypersim CC BY-SA 3.0.

Distill-Any-Depth: Apache-2.0 on the Hugging Face card (the authors' transformers ports say MIT, the code is MIT). The paper initialises the Large model from the CC-BY-NC-4.0 Depth Anything V2 Large weights; its teachers include Depth Anything V2 and it trains on unlabeled SA-1B images (research licence).
limitations: Metric checkpoints predict at most max_depth (20 m Hypersim, 80 m Virtual KITTI 2): the head is a sigmoid scaled by it. Each was fine-tuned on one synthetic domain, so indoor / outdoor scenes outside it get a wrong scale.

Distill-Any-Depth runs with this family's pipeline (short side 518, aspect kept, as the authors' transformers ports); the authors' demo squashes to 700 x 700. Their Dav2-Teacher-Large-2w-iter checkpoint is not included.
task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: a depth or inverse-depth map. `kind` (a card field, `result.kind`) says what the numbers mean: `metric` = metres; `scale_invariant`, `affine_invariant` and `affine_invariant_inverse` are relative (unknown scale or shift, not metres). Metric models that use the focal length take `model(image, intrinsics=K)` (K `[3, 3]`, pixels of the input): `metric3d-vit-large` and `da3metric-large` need it for correct metres (`da3metric-large`: metres = output x focal / 300; without `intrinsics=` a 300 px focal length is assumed, wrong for a real camera). `unidepth-v2-vitl14`, `unik3d-vitl`, `depth-pro` and MoGe estimate the camera themselves (given `intrinsics=` replace `fx`); `zoedepth-nk` and the relative models (`da3mono-large` too) take none.
